pageCache.text:
Brilliant beginnings, fantastic futures
About Us
Welcome to Faraday
An independent co-ed prep school for children aged 4-11.
Faraday is an award winning, forward-thinking prep school in East London, part of an exciting creative community on Trinity Buoy Wharf, a newly regenerated area on the banks of the River Thames.
“If excellence is what you seek, Faraday School is all you need. My family and I LOVE Faraday School, we could not have hoped for a better school!”
Hend, Reception Parent
“For us, the best aspect of Faraday School is the fact that they understand and value our son’s individuality.”
Jade, Year 5 parent
“Small, friendly school, where children get to mix across years and develop strong relationships with teachers. Strong focus on core academic skills and personal development.”
Shailen, Year 4 and Year 1 parent
“At Faraday, you will find a happy and dynamic community. It is a small and nimble school where teachers know the whole child.”
Melanie, Year 4 and Year 1 parent
School Reviews & Inspection Reports
The Week Magazine’s ‘Great City Prep’
We’ve been awarded Best of the Best Prep School for the category ‘Great City Prep’ in this year’s The Week Magazine’s ‘Independent School Guide’ Prep School edition.
‘The school, like the regenerated Wharf, has been reimagined in an innovative way that embraces heritage and modernity’
Our Story
Affordable Excellence
Faraday was founded by the New Model School Company in 2009 with a simple philanthropic aim: to provide an excellent, affordable, prep education.
Futures
Destination Schools & 11+
Excellent teaching from Reception to Year 6 creates confident children well prepared for the 11+. Our pupils regularly receive offers from London’s top senior schools.
Admissions
Visit Us
The best way to experience Faraday is to attend an open morning. Contact us with any questions you might have and we will be delighted to help. We look forward to welcoming you to our school soon.

pageCache.pageTitle: Directors and Advisors - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Directors and Advisors
We have a dedicated and highly experienced Board of Advisors and Directors who work closely with our school and support our growth.
John Ashmore MA (Edinburgh) French, has worked in a variety of industry sectors including yoghurts, toys, pet nutrition and premium spirits, where he has held positions in Marketing, Sales and General Management. Currently, he is Marketing Director Europe, Middle-East for Clearwater Seafoods, North America’s largest vertically integrated wild shellfish producer. John is a member of the Fishmongers’ Livery Company.
Alexandra Cornforth, MA (Oxon), M.Litt, rejoined the board on the 1st September and has held several Board and Trustee positions over the course of a thirty-five year career in financial services. She is currently Head of Corporate Governance for a FTSE 250 listed investment trust and is also a non executive director of an investment management company providing ethical investment solutions for charities and individuals.
Rajinder Funnell: BA, English Literature pursued a career in publishing with Hodder and Stoughton from 2001, later became a qualified early years practitioner and is a Montessori teacher, training at the Maria Montessori Institute in London. Since 2014, Rajinder has also been actively fundraising for the Rugby Portobello Trust (RPT) and, in 2022, became a Co- chair for one of their fundraising committees. The RPT is a children’s, youth and family support group, supporting the local community for over 135 years, and helping the youngest members build confidence, expand their horizons and realise their potential.
Deborah Livsey: LLB Hons (Exeter) CEO has had a 15 year career in finance which has taken her from London, to Hong Kong and Japan. She has been a governor responsible for safeguarding at Amesbury, a preparatory school in Hampshire since 2012 and a trustee of Send Family Link, a charity which supports children with a female family member in prison. She joined NMS in 2018 as its Chief Operating Officer and became CEO in July 2020.
Xavier Villers: MA (Oxon.), MSt, ACII (Chairman) Xavier spent his working career in the insurance industry in the City of London, specialising in the marine sector and extreme risks, as well as managing and integrating a number of different businesses. He now holds various non-executive roles in finance, charity, and education. He is a non-executive director of a multi academy trust which runs five primary schools over eight different sites in South London. He also resumed his own education, and recently completed a master‘s degree in historical studies focusing on 17th century English history.
Joanna Copland BA (Hons) QTS, PG Cert Dys, Mont Dip has worked in the independent sector for more than 30 years. Starting as an early years teacher, she was then Deputy Head of Thomas’s School, Clapham for 14 years before becoming Vice Principal of the Thomas’s Schools group, collaborating with the senior leaders and sharing best practice across the schools. Most recently she has been Head of Pre-Prep at Fulham School. Joanna is a member of the Educators’ Livery company and a judge for the Queen’s Commonwealth Essay competition.
Jonathan Cubitt: BA ACA is Bursar of Queen’s Gate School. Previous roles include Business Development Director of Charity HR and Finance Director of The Art Fund, the national art charity. Prior to that, he spent 15 years in accountancy, working for several leading accountancy firms.
Vania Georgeson, BA (Hons), MA, PGCE Vania is a former head teacher with a background in English and Drama, teaching in both state and independent schools. Under her 14 year headship, The Roche School in SW London became known for academic excellence, strong pastoral care, and a progressive approach to Equality, Diversity & Inclusion. She holds an MA from King’s College London/The Globe Theatre and has directed youth Shakespeare productions, and co-edited The Women Writers Handbook. Vania now runs speech classes for children and advises on parents on school placement and educational choices.
Jane Ritchie: Early Years Professional (CWDC), Cert Ed in Early Childhood Education over 40 years of experience working in Early Years Education. Jane has worked within the independent sector in advisory/management roles to nursery groups, schools, companies and individuals both in the UK and abroad. Her experience includes 9 years at the Alpha Plus Group as Director of Nurseries and Head of Early Years and owner of The Minors Nursery School, London from 1990 to August 2005.
Justin Shaw: MA (Cantab) is a former Director and Deputy Chairman of NMS, and was the company’s Chairman from its foundation in 2004 until 2008. He was also Chairman of Civitas and remains a trustee of the independent social policy think-tank. After receiving a Senior Exhibition in Philosophy at Cambridge, he studied law and was called to the Bar at Lincoln’s Inn. Justin is now a full-time writer. Recent novels include The Illumination of Merton Browne and Ten Weeks in Africa.
Natalie Smith: (Parent Advisor) LLB Hons (London School of Economics) LLM (Queen Mary University). Natalie is a parent of a child at Faraday Prep school and is also a member of the Friends of Faraday ( the School’s parent organisation). Natalie’s professional background is in law. She is a solicitor with extensive experience in both private practice and the civil service, specialising in criminal law and the criminal justice system.
Nisha Vidani: Nisha is a parent of 2 children at Maple Walk and is a successful CFO and Co-Owner of a medium sized business that exports and wholesales British and European FMCG. Nisha is a multi-award winning business executive having been awarded the Queen’s Award for Enterprise in International Trade on five occasions and featured in both the Sunday Times Fast Track 100 and International Track 200 as well as reported in JM Morgan’s Top 200 Female- Powered Businesses in both 2022 and 2023.
The Teaching and Learning Committee is the dynamo at the heart of Faraday. Its members are education specialists who oversee and drive our ambitious, knowledge-based curriculum.

Inspection Reports
Inspection Reports
Following our visit from the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) we have now received the final inspection report and we are delighted that they have recognised all of our strengths as a school.
We are especially pleased that the excellent teaching and learning at Faraday has been highlighted; it is a testament to the dedication of our staff and their commitment to achieving consistently high standards across the school.
Highlights from the Inspection Report
The inspectors commend the staff’s work across all areas including teaching and pupil well-being highlighting that: “Staff know the pupils well and actively support their individual needs” that “the pastoral provision supports pupils’ emotional wellbeing, self-esteem and confidence effectively and “teachers plan carefully and deliver interesting lessons” and “As a result of effective teaching pupils make good progress in their work”
The early years provision was commended in that it “Promotes a stimulating and nurturing learning environment which supports children’s self-esteem and confidence.” and “leaders in the early years demonstrate kindness and cheerfulness so that children learn to treat others in a friendly and respectful manner.”
The impact of our work can also be seen in recognition of pupils’ development, with inspectors noting that “pupils demonstrate consistently motivated and responsible attitudes towards their learning” and that “pupils develop a range of interests and skills”. The report highlights that “pupils develop leadership skills and learn that it is generous, kind and responsible to serve and to help others”
New Inspection Framework
Under the new inspection framework, schools no longer receive a one-word judgement; instead, reports determine whether each section of the inspection was ‘met’ or ‘unmet’. We are delighted that Faraday School met all five sections of the standards following the inspectorate’s visit in May 2026. Read the May 2026 inspection report here.

Reception 2027 Timeline
Reception Offers are made in order of date of registration, sixteen months ahead of entry. Once parents accept an offer (by agreeing to the terms of the parent contract and making payment of the acceptance deposit), children and parents attend two transition events; the Spring and Summer Stay and Plays.
MAY 2026: RECEPTION 2027 OFFERS BEGIN
Receiving & Accepting Your Offer
We begin making offers sixteen months ahead of entry into Reception. Offers are sent out in order of date of registration (with siblings of current pupils given priority).
To secure the place, payment of your acceptance deposit will be due within 10 days of your offer, along with signed agreement to terms of parent contract.
Note: A place cannot be secured without payment of the security deposit and submission of the signed acceptance form (to agree to terms of parent contract).
FEBRUARY 2027: CLOSING DATE FOR ACCEPTANCES
Closing date for Reception 2027 acceptances
Any registration received after the closing date for Reception acceptances can only be considered on a case-by-case basis.
FEBRUARY/MARCH 2027: SPRING STAY & PLAY
Meet & Greet Stay & Play
All children whose places have been accepted are invited to school in February for a stay and play session. This is an opportunity to meet teachers and potential classmates.
Parents are asked to advise the school of any relevant updates in their child’s needs (medical or developmental) since time of registration.
Please refer to our Admissions Policy.
MARCH 2027: RECEPTION 2027 FIRST TERM’S FEES
Autumn Term Fees Due
Fees for the Reception class Autumn term are due by the end of the previous Spring term.
Fees are reviewed each year by Directors. Reception 2027 Autumn fees will be due at the new 2027/28 rate.
JUNE 2027: SUMMER STAY & PLAY
Welcome back Stay and Play
Children joining Reception in September and their parents are welcomed back to school.
Children meet their new teachers and play. Parents receive information to help prepare for entry to Reception in September.
Once again, parents are asked to advise school of any relevant updates in child’s needs (medical or developmental) to help prepare for the transition.

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama and Dance - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Drama and Dance
Performing in front of an audience is an experience that can prove invaluable. Annual poetry and public-speaking competitions help the children to gain confidence when on stage, as well as enriching their understanding of literature.
Drama is timetabled for each year group once a week with a specialist teacher. Drama is exciting, fun and hugely rewarding. It builds individual confidence and requires a high degree of personal discipline, as well as developing collaboration and teamwork skills. Children also have a specialist dance lesson once a week up until Year 4.
Dance and drama tuition is provided by a qualified LAMDA teacher, who helps children gain excellent grades in the annual examinations.
The after-school dance club has competed at the National Dance Challenge three years in a row and has reached the finals twice.

Music
There are many opportunities for music-making at school. From Reception, Music is a timetabled subject taught by a specialist teacher. The curriculum includes activities that illustrate important musical concepts and terms and introduces the children to significant composers and works.
In addition to whole class music lessons, pupils may choose to learn a variety of instruments, taught by experienced peripatetic teachers, who are all professional musicians. These instruments include flute, clarinet, piano, drums and guitar.
Great importance is placed on the enjoyment and appreciation of a wide variety of music, and children are encouraged to join the school choir and music clubs such as Music Technology. Musical aptitude is studied in Year 5 and children who wish to take examinations are encouraged to do so.
Children, teachers and parents enjoy the musical performances that take place at school during the year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Fishmongers' Faraday Award - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Fishmongers’ Faraday Award 2026 Applications
Each year, the Fishmongers’ Faraday Award provides a fully funded or subsidised place for a child joining Faraday School in Year 3 or Year 4. This award is supported by The Fishmongers’ Company, one of the Great 12 Livery Companies of the City of London. We are extremely grateful to them.
The award will cover up to 100% of the school fees for a child who would otherwise be unable to attend and is currently attending a state school in Year 2 or Year 3. Special consideration will also be given to those showing creative promise but this is not a necessity.
Selection is based on the candidate’s current school report, a taster day at the school, which includes some assessments (no advance preparation is needed), and a school reference. Short-listed candidates are invited back with their parent(s) for an interview.
We look for candidates whose parents would not otherwise be able to afford an independent education and who would benefit from Faraday’s offer.
Applications for September 2026 are now closed
Previous recipients of the award have thrived at Faraday, with parents valuing the ambitious, rigorous curriculum, small class sizes, great pastoral care, after-school clubs, wonderful location and excellent senior school options.
The Fishmongers’ Faraday Award is part of our vision at the New Model School Company to broaden the reach of an excellent education to as many children as possible.
Please contact the Admissions Registrar, Stefanie Harvey, on 020 8965 7374 or by email at stefanie.harvey@newmodelschool.co.uk if you have any questions about the Award.
For more information about the work of The Fishmongers’ Company, please visit https://fishmongers.org.uk

School Awards and Reviews
Awards
The school values of Creativity, Curiosity and Community are the foundations of Faraday’s award achievements. They are a testament to the hard work and commitment from all the teaching staff and pupils and support from our parents.
INDEPENDENT SCHOOLS ASSOCIATION AWARDS
Faraday-Prep-School-ISA-Case-Study-for-Excellence-in-Fine-Arts-and-Design
ISA Journal – Faraday ‘Creativity’ Article
ISA Award for Excellence in Fine Arts and Design
“Faraday Prep is a school with creativity at its core, where the teaching of art and design is innovative, interdisciplinary and experiential. Using the city of London as an extension of its classrooms the school encourages pupils to learn about the world through an artistic lens, fusing the teaching of art with other subjects, creating a window into different cultures and perspectives. Faraday Prep School offers incredible opportunities for children to work with professional artists and have their work exhibited, and pupils take part in a range of innovative projects, with many securing art scholarships. Teaching is imaginative and innovative, and the school’s art and design offering is outstanding.”
OTHER INDUSTRY AWARDS
Faraday was named Independent Prep School of the Year 2024 by Independent School Parent Magazine and the Telegraph Media Group at an awards ceremony in central London on 8th October.
The awards were chaired by Dr Helen Wright and supported by independent judges, leading headteachers and representatives of the professional associations. Presenting our award, the judges praised Faraday’s commitment to innovation, our breadth of educational experiences and excellent pastoral care for our children. Mr Motion and Miss Drummonds were enormously proud to receive the award on behalf of the school community:
“It is heartening to see the hard work of everyone at the school acknowledged in this way and I would like to thank Faraday staff for their craft and commitment. Perhaps most importantly, this award reflects the wonderful community spirit that makes our school so special. We are immensely grateful to you, our parents, for your collaboration and support.”
The Week’s Best of the Best Prep Guide Awards Faraday Prep school ‘Great City Prep’
This forward-thinking prep school in East London is part of Trinity Buoy Wharf, a creative community on the bank of the River Thames.
The school, like the regenerated Wharf, has been reimagined in an innovative way that embraces heritage and modernity – pupils are taught in a mixture of historic buildings and shipping container classrooms, and a roof-top playground provides spectacular views of the Thames, the O2 arena and Faraday Lighthouse.
The Wharf is home to many household names in the arts, such as The Prince’s Foundation, English National Opera and The Big Draw and the school buzzes with the same spirit of artistic endeavour.
Collaborations take place every term, from pupils creating their own animations with Isle of Dogs and Fantastic Mr Fox filmmaker Tim Allen to learning alongside sculptor Ros Burgin, workshops with resident weaver Daniel Harris and taking part in Thames Heritage projects. with local artists.
It is no surprise that Faraday students have entered the Royal Academy Young Artists and The Fourth Plinth Awards.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our core values:
Curiosity to seek knowledge and love learning
Creativity to innovate and collaborate
Community to foster a sense of belonging in our school and the world around us
Our Vision:
To provide an excellent, forward-thinking education that inspires and challenges every child
To recognise the value of knowledge and how it helps children to understand their world and the positive difference they can make
To instil a love of learning through a broad, exciting curriculum with strong foundations in literacy and numeracy
To empower pupils with a sense of belonging, allowing them to fulfil their potential and grow in confidence
To value the diversity of our community by celebrating all religions, beliefs, backgrounds and cultures
To offer a great value education, enabling as many families as possible to benefit from our ‘not-for-profit’ ethos
Our Approach
We believe that learning should be rich, varied and exciting. It should be taught creatively and tailored individually.
The New Model School Company (NMS) offers a great value education. We are forward thinking, sustainability is central to our ethos and our school buildings are modern and innovative. We deliver an ambitious knowledge-based curriculum that is taught in a creative way. We are confident that what we teach, and how we teach it, is truly excellent.
By embedding our pupils learning in the community, using the best of what the neighbourhood has to offer, whether that be Roundwood Park or the River Thames, we provide our pupils with a deeper learning experience.
From Year 1, NMS pupils are taught content-rich subjects rooted in the arts and sciences. We believe that it is through acquiring knowledge that a child is inspired to become a lifelong learner. This emphasis also provides our children with the solid foundations to grasp a wider range of subjects later in their formal education.
A good curriculum costs no more to teach than a bad one.
Creativity and curiosity are two of our key values. Our pupils are given the opportunity to take part in many different sports and a wide range of arts such as Art, Music, Drama and Dance, all taught by specialist teachers.
Regular residential trips, excursions and activities within the local community enhance our pupils’ educational experience and help them to develop their confidence and independence. Each school also runs an extensive range of after-school clubs each term, ranging from Robotics Club to Art Club, from Science Club to Athletics Club.
We believe that our approach ensures that our children’s outlook and horizons develop beyond their everyday experience.
The NMS Teaching and Learning Committee oversees the curriculum. To find out more about its work, click here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception Entry 2027 & Beyond - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Reception Entry
The main point of entry to Faraday is at four years old when children join Reception. We are an academically non-selective school which means that we don’t have daunting tests for the children joining us in Reception. You can see our Early Years pupils in action by booking onto an Open Morning.
Reception 2027 Complete a pupil registration form and the registrar will be in touch. Offers for places for entry to Faraday in Reception 2027 will be sent in order of date of registration. For more details email admissions@faradayschool.co.uk
Complete the registration form and make payment of the registration fee
Once the registration form and fee have been received, you will receive confirmation that your child has been added to the registration list for their Reception year of entry (children must be 4 years old on 1st September in the Autumn term that they join Reception)
Any registration received after the closing date for Reception acceptances (February prior to entry) can only be considered on a case-by-case basis.
Book onto an Open Morning and visit the school
You can book onto an open morning before you register if you prefer.
The open mornings last approximately one hour and are an opportunity to meet the Head Teacher and have a tour of the school led by our Year Six pupils.
Reception offers are sent out approximately sixteen months ahead of entry
Keep your contact details up to date with the registrar so that you don’t miss out when the offer process begins as contact will be made by email.
Parents are asked to keep the registrar updated with any relevant information regarding their child’s health and development in the period following registration, as detailed in the Admissions Policy.
To accept a child’s offer of a place, parents pay the acceptance deposit and return the signed acceptance form, agreeing to the terms and conditions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Art and Design
Creativity in all its forms is central to the ethos of Faraday. Children learn to appreciate and value images and artefacts across time and cultures and learn to understand the contexts in which they were made.
A creative vibe is felt as soon as you step through the school gate
In Art and Design, pupils reflect critically on their own and others’ work, judging quality and meaning. They learn to think and act as artists, craftspeople and designers, working creatively and intelligently. They develop an appreciation of art, craft and design, and their role in the creative and cultural industries that enrich their lives.
At Faraday School pupils have an arts-rich education and opportunities to work on projects with artists, perform and have their work exhibited
– Artsmark, Arts Council 2023
We aim to encourage the development of imagination, original thought and personal expression.
“Arts and culture are linked to wider learning opportunities, for example through the Thames Festival Bubble Town project which included history and geography.” – Artsmark, Arts Council 2023.
For exceptionally talented artists, we offer a portfolio club to help pupils prepare for art scholarships. Our pupils are regularly offered art scholarships for senior school.

English
Reading is the gateway to knowledge. Once a child can read fluently and independently, they widen their world. We therefore place great emphasis on teaching children to read as early as possible in their school careers and encourage it as a hobby and a tool throughout their time with us.
Fiction, plays and poems form an integral part of many lessons, with not only the reading and comprehension of a text being significant, but also how theme, style, structure and language are used. Whole class, small group and independent reading activities enhance speaking, listening and writing tasks, develop reading skills and encourage personal enjoyment and enthusiasm for reading.
We teach reading by means of synthetic phonics, the traditional method of associating letters with sounds that has been proven to be the most effective way to teach children to read, including children with learning difficulties. Spelling, handwriting, vocabulary, grammatical accuracy and creative style are all developed to high standards. The children’s written work is regularly shared and celebrated in House meetings and assemblies.
We have many events in the school year that serve to promote literacy, including the much-coveted poetry competition, readathon and public speaking competition. We also invite authors to speak to the children and ensure there are workshops that show them how storytelling, writing and reading can be used to inspire others and make a difference.
Our aim is to have all children reading independently and feeling able to express themselves in writing by the end of Year 1. To achieve this, we ask for the support of parents, who are encouraged to read to – and with – their children every day. Working in partnership with parents is very important to us and helps the children to progress rapidly.

Humanities
History provides valuable insights into the world we live in today and Geography gives us a sense of place in the world.
History
History provides valuable insights into the world we live in today. By understanding the past, our children can grasp how societies, cultures, and civilizations have evolved over time. This knowledge helps them make sense of current events and appreciate the significance of certain developments or issues.
At school, our history curriculum promotes critical thinking skills. Analysing historical events, causes, and consequences encourages pupils to examine evidence, evaluate different perspectives, and develop their own informed opinions.
By studying the experiences of different individuals and societies throughout history, children can develop an understanding of diverse perspectives and cultures. This fosters tolerance, respect, and an appreciation for the shared humanity of people from different backgrounds.
Areas covered by the curriculum include:
Geography
Geography gives us a sense of place in the world.
As children become familiar with globes, maps and atlases, they appreciate both their local environment, as well as their relation to the country and continent they inhabit, and the world beyond. Geography helps us to understand why settlements grew up where they did, how the world’s resources are accessed and transported, and what processes shape the world around us. Our approach emphasises human as well as physical geography and the study of the cultures, languages, arts and industries of the many and varied places on earth.
Religious Education
Religious Education aims to enable pupils to develop an understanding of other cultures and lifestyles.
Pupils have an opportunity to explore stories and beliefs from a variety of religions, including Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism. Pupils also study Philosophy and ask ‘big’ questions in their weekly Philosophy Fox discussions.
The curriculum is delivered creatively by teachers using drama, discussions, debates, visits to places of worship and sessions with outside speakers.

French is an integral part of the curriculum for all pupils from Reception onwards. Learning a foreign language in depth and studying a foreign culture is invaluable in broadening the mind and teaching the pupils to develop their understanding of linguistics.

Optional after-school clubs offer pupils the chance to learn other languages, such as Japanese, Spanish and Mandarin.

Science
We see Science as an essential discipline for young children. Our curriculum will lay the foundation for pupils to understand what the discipline of Science tells us about the world. We aim to ignite children’s love for science by showing them what fascinating things the human race has learned about the world.
We go beyond the national curriculum in what we teach. Children are introduced to the inner workings of the human body, animals and the environments they live in, plants and their features, forces of nature, and what lies beyond the visible world. Children are taught to apply their knowledge and conduct their own scientific enquiries to answer questions, working scientifically to develop essential skills. Every opportunity is taken to allow the children to experience the practical aspects of the subject.
Science teaches an understanding of natural phenomena. We aim to stimulate a child’s curiosity about finding out why things happen in the way they do. The subject teaches methods of enquiry and investigation to stimulate creative thought. Children learn to ask scientific questions and begin to appreciate the way that Science will affect their future on a personal, national and global level.
Our science curriculum builds knowledge incrementally year-on-year to revisit and build upon children’s knowledge and understanding of key concepts. Pupils also study the lives and achievements of a diverse range of scientists including Lewis Howard Latimer, Thomas Edison and Jabir ibn Hayyan. Their disciplinary knowledge will flourish over time, enabling them to see the importance of Science as a subject, how it translates into the world of research and work, what scientists do and how they impact upon our lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Friends of Faraday - Faraday Prep School
pageCache.text:
Friends of Faraday
The Friends of Faraday is our very active and creative parent organisation, who are a vital part of the school community. All parents are encouraged to take part and their involvement strengthens the family feel of Faraday, playing a crucial role in the ongoing success of the school.
The Friends of Faraday organise many pupil and family events and activities during the school year. Previous events include: upper and lower school discos, film nights, bake sales, and Christmas lunch for children and staff. The Friends also organise an annual Christmas card project, which offers parents the opportunity to purchase mugs, cards and gift-wrap with their child’s bespoke design. Twice yearly, the Friends host a Book Fair, which raises funds that have helped to expand Faraday’s library, keeping up with the children’s appetite for new books that can be read both in the classroom and at home.
New and existing parents are always welcome to reach out to the Friends of Faraday with any questions about school life and are welcome to help with organising events at any point during their child’s time at Faraday. We are excited to watch the Friends of Faraday grow with each new Reception intake.
